prompt:
Extract the one contact record from the note. Use only its label–value lines, which may be shuffled and separated by a colon, equals sign, or tab. Never use surrounding notes, signatures, email domains, or company suffixes to infer field values; suffixes may be used for the explicit swap below.

Return one bare JSON object with exactly the keys name, phone, email, company, country. Every value is a string or JSON null. No other text, Markdown, or keys.

Trim values and collapse whitespace runs to one space. Treat absent or empty values and these case-insensitive placeholders as null: -, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD. Do not guess. The sole missing-value exception is the international-phone country fallback below.

Assign email and phone by content regardless of label: @ identifies email; at least seven digits and only digits, spaces, or + - ( ) . / after removing a leading tel: and a trailing extension identify phone. Extensions may use ext., ext, x, #, or extension followed by digits. Use the country line for country. If the name value ends in a listed legal suffix and the company value does not, swap those values before cleanup.

Name: split at the first comma, if present, and move the part after it before the part preceding it. Remove leading Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx, Prof, ignoring case and an optional dot. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the remainder of each space- or hyphen-separated part. Preserve Unicode letters and diacritics under casing; never transliterate.

Company: remove a trailing legal suffix and its optional preceding comma, case-insensitively: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the remainder of each space-separated word.

Email: strip surrounding angle brackets and the mailto: prefix, including when the prefix is inside the brackets. Lowercase the address without otherwise changing its characters.

Country: convert English, Swedish, or German names or alpha-2/alpha-3 codes, in any case, to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Aliases: UK and Great Britain → GB; Holland → NL; USA and U.S.A. → US; Türkiye → TR; Czech Republic → CZ.

Phone: after stripping tel: and the extension, detect an international number by a leading + or 00, ignoring an opening parenthesis. For international numbers, convert 00 to +, remove (0) and all spaces, dashes, dots, slashes and parentheses, and keep the written calling code. If the country line is missing, empty, or a placeholder, fill country from that calling code only if it identifies a single country. Shared codes such as +1 and +7 leave country null. A present country stays as written after ISO conversion even if it disagrees with the international phone. For a national number, strip formatting, remove one leading trunk 0, and prepend + and the normalized country's calling code; if country is missing, return null for phone. Output every non-null phone in E.164: + followed only by calling-code and national significant digits. Trim final strings.
